claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is in an as-cast state.
The initial alloy has a homogeneous microstructure.
The initial alloy has minimal pre-existing defects.
Above approximately 500 °C, thermal energy enhances anharmonic lattice vibrations in HfNbTaTiZr.
Enhanced anharmonic lattice vibrations cause a nonlinear increase in interatomic distances and lattice parameters.
The nonlinear lattice expansion reduces the effective elastic constants or elastic moduli.
The reduction in elastic response modifies the alloy's stress–strain behavior relative to room temperature.
The predicted elevated-temperature responses occur independently of major microstructural changes.
Above approximately 500 °C, in situ XRD is predicted to show lattice parameters increasing nonlinearly relative to a room-temperature extrapolation.
Above approximately 500 °C, the elastic moduli are predicted to be lower than room-temperature extrapolations.
Above approximately 500 °C, stress–strain curves are predicted to deviate from room-temperature behavior.
Room-temperature lattice parameters, elastic moduli, and stress–strain behavior will serve as the comparison baseline.
The proposed test range is room temperature to 800 °C.
Identical specimen geometry and atmosphere will be used across test conditions.
EBSD and TEM monitoring of grain boundaries and dislocations can determine whether microstructural evolution is a major alternative driver of the mechanical response.
Purely linear thermal expansion together with no nonlinear change in elastic or stress–strain behavior would falsify the proposed anharmonicity mechanism.
Significant microstructural alterations that correlate with the mechanical response would falsify the claim that anharmonic lattice vibrations are the primary driver.
